_slice: BC school tax, local-government statistics and unconditional grants
_note: Closes three Alberta-parallel gaps: (1) provincial compilation of municipal financial data (LGDE → published schedules), (2) education property-tax mechanism that rests on BC Assessment, (3) formula-driven unconditional grants that weight population and assessment. No equalized-assessment step exists; assessment is already uniform province-wide.

proposed_reports.title: Local Government Statistics (Municipal General and Financial Statistics Schedules)
proposed_reports.publisher: Ministry of Housing and Municipal Affairs (Province of British Columbia)
proposed_reports.description: Annual compilation of standardized financial and statistical data submitted by every municipality and regional district via the Local Government Data Entry (LGDE) system. Covers assets, liabilities, long-term debt, revenues, expenditures, tangible capital assets, reserve funds, tax rates and tax burden. Closest functional equivalent to Alberta's Municipal Financial and Statistical Data / FIR compilation. Data due from local governments by 15 May; published in numbered schedules.

proposed_reports.title: Provincial School Tax Rates (Residential and Non-Residential Orders in Council)
proposed_reports.publisher: Province of British Columbia (Orders in Council under the School Act)
proposed_reports.description: Annual residential school-tax rates set by Order in Council for each school district (formula weights number of residences and total residential assessed value) and province-wide non-residential class rates. Includes the Additional School Tax on high-value residential properties (threshold currently $3 million). Rates applied to net taxable assessed values determined by BC Assessment; municipalities and the Surveyor of Taxes collect and remit.

proposed_reports.title: Small Community Grants (Unconditional)
proposed_reports.publisher: Ministry of Housing and Municipal Affairs
proposed_reports.description: Annual unconditional operating grants to municipalities with population up to approximately 19 000. Formula under the Local Government Grants Regulation comprises a base amount, an equalization component driven by assessment weighting factor (provincial average assessment per person divided by the municipality's), and a population component. Parallel to Alberta-style population- and assessment-weighted transfers.

proposed_reports.title: Local Government Grants Act [RSBC 1996] c. 275
proposed_reports.description: Enabling statute for unconditional and conditional grants to municipalities and regional districts. Section 3 authorises unconditional grants to be calculated on population, total expenditures/revenues, converted value of land and improvements (i.e. assessment), or other prescribed bases.

dependencies.basis: Community Charter s. 167 requires every municipality to prepare annual financial statements and submit them (together with tax-rate information) to the Inspector of Municipalities by 15 May; the LGDE forms and resulting published schedules are the standardized product of that statutory reporting obligation.
dependencies.evidence_quote: All local governments in B.C. must submit financial statements and tax rate information by May 15 each year by submitting: Financial plans, Audited financial statements, Tax rate bylaws, Local Government Data Entry (LGDE) forms, LGDE tax forms. Once reviewed by the ministry this information is published in statistical schedules.

dependencies.basis: Residential school-tax rates for each district are set using total residential assessed value in the district; the Additional School Tax applicability and taxable amount are determined from the net taxable value of the dwelling property as assessed by BC Assessment.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Each year the province sets the residential school tax rate for each school district and is based equally on: 1) The total number of residences in the district 2) The total residential assessed value in the district. BC Assessment determines if the additional school tax rate applies to your property.

dependencies.basis: The grant program is authorised by the Local Government Grants Act and the detailed formula (base + assessment-weighting equalization + population) is prescribed in the Local Government Grants Regulation.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The Local Government Grants Act and Local Government Grants Regulation have detailed information on provincial funding for local governments. Grant amounts are based on a formula that incorporates a base amount, population and assessment values.

dependencies.basis: The equalization component of the Small Community Grant uses an assessment weighting factor defined as provincial average assessment per person divided by the municipality's per-person assessment (converted value of land and improvements).
dependencies.evidence_quote: "assessment" in relation to a jurisdiction means the converted value of land and improvements, as defined in section 1 of the Schedule to the Community Charter, in the jurisdiction; "assessment weighting factor" in relation to a municipality means the provincial assessment value divided by the per person assessment of the municipality

dependencies.basis: The population component of the grant formula uses the municipality's mean population (derived from census / official estimates).
dependencies.evidence_quote: Grant amounts are based on a formula that incorporates a base amount, population and assessment values.
